## Frontend Defaults

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-roles.sh from each rule's strength line. Change the rule, then rebuild; do not edit this file. -->

Each line is one rule: its title, its one sentence, and the file that holds it.

- **Inject collaborators instead of passing an options bag.** Inject runtime collaborators via their ports; pass only identity and per-instance config as arguments. [`frontend/inject-collaborators-instead-of-passing-an-options-bag.md`]
- **Pass local dependencies as props and events.** Communicate between a parent component and its child via props and events, not a provided port. [`frontend/pass-local-dependencies-as-props-and-events.md`]
- **Keep composition roots free of business logic.** A composition root (`app.vue`, layout, or page) creates composables, provides ports, and composes components — no business logic or inline pure transforms. [`frontend/keep-composition-roots-free-of-business-logic.md`]
- **Do not hide composition in global setup.** Never wire page-scoped composables or ports in the app shell (`app.vue`); put composition there only for genuinely app-wide capabilities. [`frontend/do-not-hide-composition-in-global-setup.md`]
- **Import across page layers in one direction.** Imports between page folders point one way: `logic/` imports none of the others, `ports/` imports only `logic/` (plus `useProvideInject`), `adapters/` imports only `logic/` and `ports/`, and components never import `adapters/`. [`frontend/import-across-page-layers-in-one-direction.md`]
- **Keep logic free of framework imports.** Files in `logic/` are pure TypeScript: no imports from `vue`, `nuxt`, `#imports`, or any framework package. [`frontend/keep-logic-free-of-framework-imports.md`]
- **Put pure functions in logic.** Anything that can be a pure function lives in `logic/`: transforms, immutable data shaping, mapping a server value to a label, colour, icon, or order, and checks on client state with their limits taken from the DTO. [`frontend/put-pure-functions-in-logic.md`]
- **Keep a port file to its type and pair.** A port file holds only the port type and its `[injectX, provideX]` pair from `useProvideInject`; it imports only types and that helper, never `provide`, `inject`, or values from `vue`. [`frontend/keep-a-port-file-to-its-type-and-pair.md`]
- **Shape a port around operations, not DTOs.** Give each feature concern one port shaped around the UI's needed operations — not one port per function, DTO, or generated client. [`frontend/shape-a-port-around-operations-not-dtos.md`]
- **Expose refs only from a provided context.** A capability port exposes plain values and functions; only a provided context (a reactive view-model for a Vue subtree) exposes `Ref` or `ComputedRef`, and is not presented as framework-neutral. [`frontend/expose-refs-only-from-a-provided-context.md`]
- **Create port pairs with the typed helper.** Create every port's `[injectX, provideX]` pair with `useProvideInject`: `inject` throws outside a provider, and `provide` returns the concrete implementation rather than the narrowed port type. [`frontend/create-port-pairs-with-the-typed-helper.md`]
- **Inject the port, not its implementation.** Depend on a provided capability by importing `injectX` from `ports/`, never the implementation composable or adapter. [`frontend/inject-the-port-not-its-implementation.md`]
- **Keep adapters free of Vue and presentation state.** An adapter translates between a port and HTTP, a generated client, storage, or a platform API; it holds no presentation state, and a pure adapter imports nothing from Vue or Nuxt. [`frontend/keep-adapters-free-of-vue-and-presentation-state.md`]
- **Let a stateful composable implement the port.** When an implementation is already reactive and stateful, let the composable return the port shape and provide it directly; add a pure adapter only when pure logic is worth separating. [`frontend/let-a-stateful-composable-implement-the-port.md`]
- **Check an implementation with satisfies.** Verify a composable meets its port with `implementation satisfies Port`, not a `(): Port` return annotation, when it exposes extra members only the composition root needs. [`frontend/check-an-implementation-with-satisfies.md`]
- **Give a composable one capability.** A composable may hold reactive state, client calls, side effects, and local UI orchestration, but returns a surface for one capability rather than several. [`frontend/give-a-composable-one-capability.md`]
- **Keep components presentational.** A component renders data, holds local UI state, emits events, and may inject a provided capability; it never calls a generated client, runs workflows, constructs infrastructure, or bypasses its composition root. [`frontend/keep-components-presentational.md`]
- **Call the generated client in the implementing composable.** Call the generated API client inside the composable or adapter that implements the capability, never in a component. [`frontend/call-the-generated-client-in-the-implementing-composable.md`]
- **Colocate page code with its page.** Code used by one page lives in that page's folder, under `components/`, `composables/`, `logic/`, `ports/`, and `adapters/`. [`frontend/colocate-page-code-with-its-page.md`]
- **Never import another page's local code.** A page or layout subtree never imports from another page's local folders (`components/`, `composables/`, `logic/`, `ports/`, `adapters/`). [`frontend/never-import-another-pages-local-code.md`]
- **Promote shared code to a feature or shared.** When multiple subtrees need a product capability, move its port and pure logic to `app/features/<feature>/` (and ownerless code to `app/shared/`); keep single-root implementations beside that root, and move multi-root implementations into the feature. [`frontend/promote-shared-code-to-a-feature-or-shared.md`]
- **Import a feature only through its index.** Import a feature only through `app/features/<feature>/index.ts`, never its internal files. [`frontend/import-a-feature-only-through-its-index.md`]
- **Keep page state out of global stores.** Do not use a global store as the default home for state, or to carry unrelated concerns between components; state that one page or layout owns lives in a composable at that root. [`frontend/keep-page-state-out-of-global-stores.md`]
- **Call useState only inside a composable.** Call Nuxt `useState(` only inside `composables/`; the composable owns the key, and all other layers (components, pages, plugins, logic, adapters) call the composable, never the string key. [`frontend/call-usestate-only-inside-a-composable.md`]
- **Build frontends as single-page apps.** Build a frontend as a single-page app and do not use server-rendering idioms. [`frontend/build-frontends-as-single-page-apps.md`]
- **State the user's job before designing controls.** Before designing controls, state who is acting, their goal, the decisions required, which depend on earlier ones, and what they must see to trust the result, then derive page structure from that. [`ui/state-the-users-job-before-designing-controls.md`]
- **Make the headings read as the user's journey.** A setup flow's headings alone, read top to bottom, tell the user's journey in their terms, not the implementation's. [`ui/make-the-headings-read-as-the-users-journey.md`]
- **Ask for outcomes, not mechanisms.** A control asks a question the user can answer from what they know about their own work, not one about the mechanism behind it. [`ui/ask-for-outcomes-not-mechanisms.md`]
- **Collapse technical variants into one user action.** Offer one action for one user intention and let its editor handle technical variants. [`ui/collapse-technical-variants-into-one-user-action.md`]
- **Order by the user journey.** Order decisions as the user reasons about the task (context, primary choice, required config, edge cases, review, confirm); never ask a later question before its context is set. [`ui/order-by-the-user-journey.md`]
- **Keep dependent controls beside their choice.** Keep a dependent control next to the choice that reveals it. [`ui/keep-dependent-controls-beside-their-choice.md`]
- **Group one decision at a time.** Each visual section answers one user question: never group controls because they share a backend object, and never split one decision across cards because separate operations or models implement it. [`ui/group-one-decision-at-a-time.md`]
- **Present the same decision the same way everywhere.** Present a decision that is the same in concept with the same control, wording, and order wherever it appears. [`ui/present-the-same-decision-the-same-way-everywhere.md`]
- **Make the default legible.** A selected default says what it will do, and where its consequences are not obvious, says why it suits. [`ui/make-the-default-legible.md`]
- **Make every default safe.** Offer a recommended default where the product has a safe, common choice, and never a default that silently overwrites data, widens access, or loses information. [`ui/make-every-default-safe.md`]
- **Prefer progressive disclosure.** Keep the common path immediately clear and reveal advanced options only when selected or needed; never show every technical mode or empty advanced editor on load. [`ui/prefer-progressive-disclosure.md`]
- **Hide a choice that has only one option.** Hide a dropdown whose only option is its current default, keep it mounted until a second option exists, and state the default as text if not obvious. [`ui/hide-a-choice-that-has-only-one-option.md`]
- **Pick a required choice that has one candidate.** Pre-select a required choice that has only one candidate. [`ui/pick-a-required-choice-that-has-one-candidate.md`]
- **Keep a target picker visible with one candidate.** Keep a target picker (stage, list, column) visible even with one candidate, and keep a lone stale "(unavailable)" option visible too. [`ui/keep-a-target-picker-visible-with-one-candidate.md`]
- **Use domain language.** Use the words users meet in their work rather than words from the implementation, unless the intended user genuinely uses the technical word, and introduce an unavoidable technical term through familiar language. [`ui/use-domain-language.md`]
- **Explain consequences, not system events.** A label says what will happen to the user's work, not what the system does internally. [`ui/explain-consequences-not-system-events.md`]
- **Use help text for the user's next question.** Supporting text explains a material consequence or answers the user's likely next question; it never restates the label. [`ui/use-help-text-for-the-users-next-question.md`]
- **Show the result.** Where the user would otherwise have to run the rules in their head, show the resulting outcome: the final file path, generated filename, recipient summary, permission effect, schedule, filter result, or mapped data. [`ui/show-the-result.md`]
- **Keep a preview live and marked as an example.** A preview updates as the configuration changes, uses representative sample values, and is clearly marked as an example, not a live operation. [`ui/keep-a-preview-live-and-marked-as-an-example.md`]
- **Make the final summary match what will happen.** The final review or summary states exactly what will happen when the user confirms. [`ui/make-the-final-summary-match-what-will-happen.md`]
- **Treat disabled states as explanations.** A disabled control must explain why it is disabled and how to enable it: hide it until its prerequisite is chosen, show the prerequisite beside it, or state in plain words what to do. [`ui/treat-disabled-states-as-explanations.md`]
- **Describe the action, not the step number.** Guidance names the action the user must take; a step number is only a secondary aid, since numbering changes and users think in tasks. [`ui/describe-the-action-not-the-step-number.md`]
- **Follow the GOV.UK Design System for open details.** Where accessibility, formatting, display, or validation is unspecified, follow the matching GOV.UK Design System component or pattern and name it in the spec or summary. [`ui/follow-the-govuk-design-system-for-open-details.md`]
